strict.criterion: Effective functional models cover all major human brain regions and their integrated cognitive operation by the close of the mid-2020s (December 2026).
strict.rationale: The mid-2020s window closes at the end of 2026, so this prediction remains pending as of October 15, 2026. Current neuroscience—human cortical parcellation, a mouse cell atlas, and a fruit-fly connectome—represents partial progress far short of a functional whole-human-brain model.

evidence.title: NIH: Complete cell map of a whole mammalian brain
evidence.note: Mouse cell atlas, not a functional emulation of the entire human brain.

evidence.title: Dorkenwald et al.: Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain
evidence.note: Adult fruit-fly connectome. Species, wiring map and functional cognitive model must not be conflated.

evidence.title: Glasser et al.: A multi-modal parcellation of human cerebral cortex
evidence.note: 180 cortical areas per hemisphere; direct evidence of improved regional brain understanding, not whole-brain functional reconstruction.

reference.criterion: Effective functional models cover all major human brain regions and their integrated operation, not just a wiring atlas, by the close of the mid-2020s (December 2026).
reference.rationale: Applying the same window-endpoint rule used for other approximate periods ('early 2030s' → 2033), 'mid-2020s' closes on December 31, 2026, keeping this pending at the October 15, 2026 snapshot. Current evidence (human cortical parcellation, mouse cell atlas, fruit-fly connectome) shows meaningful partial progress well short of whole-human-brain modeling.
